title: Lesson 35 - Data quality at load: validation, dedup, transformation, stewardship, testing
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend appropriate techniques and methods for ensuring high data quality at load time, including validation, deduplication, transformation, stewardship, and testing before and during migration.

questions.question: A migration source has inconsistent date formats and duplicate customers. What should happen BEFORE loading into Salesforce?
options: Load and then fix duplicates with duplicate rules
Profile, cleanse/normalize formats, and deduplicate before loading
questions.explanation: Quality is designed before load: profile, cleanse, and dedupe first; loading then fixing (A) is costlier and risks bad merges, and the others do not address quality.

questions.question: Which TWO elements make up a reliable migration quality gate?
options: A page layout matching the source fields
Reconciliation of source vs loaded counts plus a rejects/error file
Disabling target validation rules during load
questions.explanation: A versioned mapping (A) and count reconciliation with an error file (C) are the quality gates; layouts are irrelevant and disabling validation defeats quality.

questions.question: Why run a dry-run load at representative volume in a full sandbox?
options: To surface LDV performance and data-quality issues and reconcile before production cutover
To avoid needing a mapping document
questions.explanation: Volume-representative dry runs expose scale/quality problems and enable reconciliation before cutover; the other options are not reasons.
